tex_content.html:
Proposition
[the bracket of $\mathrm{iso}$ from the curvature]

Source: petersen:page-0384, petersen:page-0385 ↗ def:pet-ch10-tp-decomposition 1. ch10:10.1.4Under subsection 1.3, the bracket is determined by $R_p$:

  1. If $X,Y\in T_pM$, then $[X,Y]=R(X,Y)\in s_p$.

  2. If $X\in T_pM$ and $S\in s_p$, then $[X,S]=-S(X)\in T_pM$.

  3. If $S,T\in s_p$, then $[S,T]=-(S\circ T-T\circ S)\in s_p$.

Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch10-lie-bracket-curvature \sketch Use torsion-freeness together with

\[ [ abla X, abla Y](V)+ abla _V[X,Y]=R(X,Y)V. \]

If $X,Y\in t_p$, their first derivatives vanish at $p$, so $[X,Y]_p=0$ and $( abla [X,Y])_p=R(X_p,Y_p)$, proving the first formula. If $X\in t_p$ and $S=( abla Y)_p$ for $Y\in \mathrm{iso}_p$, evaluation of $[X,Y]= abla _YX- abla _XY$ gives $[X,S]=-S(X)$. Finally, for isotropy fields with derivatives $S,T$, both values vanish at $p$; the displayed curvature identity reduces to $( abla [X,Y])_p=-(S\circ T-T\circ S)$.

□
